# Voxide Integration Guide

A deeper walkthrough than the README: framework-specific setup, patterns, and gotchas.

---

## 1. Get your key

Create a project in the Voxide dashboard and copy its **publishable key** (`vox_pub_…`). It's safe to ship in client code. While developing, `localhost` is always allowed; before going live, add your production domain to the project's **domain whitelist**.

---

## 2. Next.js (App Router)

`<VoxideWidget>` is a client component. Render it from one:

```tsx
// app/_components/Assistant.tsx
"use client";
import { VoxideClient, VoxideWidget } from "@voxide/react";
import { useRouter } from "next/navigation";
import { useMemo } from "react";

export default function Assistant() {
  const router = useRouter();
  const ai = useMemo(() => {
    const client = new VoxideClient({ publicKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_VOXIDE_KEY! });
    client.enableNavigation(router); // gives the agent a `navigate` tool
    client.register({
      searchProducts: {
        description: "Search the catalogue by keyword.",
        params: { query: { type: "string", required: true } },
        handler: ({ query }) => router.push(`/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`),
      },
    });
    return client;
  }, [router]);

  return <VoxideWidget client={ai} theme="auto" accentColor="#FF6600" />;
}
```

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx  → render <Assistant /> once, near the end of <body>
```

> Create the client inside `useMemo` (or a module singleton) so a re-render doesn't spin up a new client each time.

---

## 3. Vite / CRA / Remix

Same code, minus the `"use client"` directive:

```tsx
import { VoxideClient, VoxideWidget } from "@voxide/react";

const ai = new VoxideClient({ publicKey: import.meta.env.VITE_VOXIDE_KEY });
ai.register({ /* ... */ });

export default function App() {
  return <><YourApp /><VoxideWidget client={ai} /></>;
}
```

---

## 4. Designing good actions

- **Describe the outcome, not the implementation.** `"Add an item to the cart"` beats `"POST /cart"`.
- **Mark required params.** The agent will ask the user for anything `required` that's missing instead of guessing.
- **Return useful data.** Whatever your `handler` returns is sent back to the model, so it can speak the result:
  ```ts
  checkStock: {
    description: "Check whether a product is in stock.",
    params: { sku: { type: "string", required: true } },
    handler: async ({ sku }) => ({ inStock: await stock(sku) }), // agent says "yes, in stock"
  }
  ```
- **Flag destructive actions** with `dangerous: true` so the user must confirm before it runs.

---

## 5. Scopes (per-page capabilities)

Keep the toolset small and relevant by scoping actions to routes:

```ts
ai.register({
  applyCoupon: { description: "Apply a coupon.", scope: "/checkout", handler },
  deleteAccount: { description: "Delete the account.", scope: "/settings", dangerous: true, handler },
});

// tell the SDK where the user is (call on every route change)
ai.setActiveRoute(location.pathname);
```

`scope: "/shop/*"` matches any sub-route of `/shop`. `"global"` (the default) is always available.

---

## 6. Live UI state

Give the agent context without prompt-stuffing:

```ts
ai.bindState(() => ({
  cartItems: cart.length,
  currentPage: location.pathname,
  isLoggedIn: !!user,
}));
```

The snapshot is attached to every message and tool call.

---

## 7. Custom confirmation UI

```ts
ai.onConfirmation(async (action, args) => {
  return await myConfirmDialog({ title: "Confirm", body: action.description });
});
```

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Widget shows "Assistant unavailable" | Domain not whitelisted, or project paused, in the dashboard. |
| Mic never activates | Browser blocked mic permission, or the page isn't served over HTTPS (required off-localhost). |
| Agent talks but never calls tools | Action `description`s are too vague, or the action's `scope` doesn't match the current route. |
| "publicKey does not look like a Voxide key" warning | You passed the wrong key — publishable keys start with `vox_pub_`. |

---

## 9. Self-hosting the backend

By default the SDK points at the Voxide hosted backend. To run your own proxy, pass `baseUrl`:

```ts
new VoxideClient({ publicKey: "vox_pub_...", baseUrl: "https://voice.yourcompany.com" });
```

Your backend must expose `GET /api/sdk/init`, `POST /api/sdk/manifest`, and the `ws(s)://…/api/sdk/live` WebSocket (see the `voxide-ws-server` reference implementation).
